transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I'm here. I just... well, I'm here because I feel like I'm always running a bit hot, you know? Like I just can't seem to shut the motor off. It's usually fine, I mean, I'm a firefighter, so having energy is a good thing, right? But lately, it's just... it's been getting me into a little bit of trouble at the firehouse. Nothing too crazy, I don't think, but enough that I figured I should probably talk to someone about it. Does that make sense?
Have you had any distinct periods when your mood was abnormally elevated or irritable compared with your usual self?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I try to be a pretty positive guy, you know? Just generally upbeat. I wouldn't say it's ever abnormal or anything like that, just... regular good moods, I guess? 

And I really try hard not to get irritable with people. Living and working at the firehouse, you kind of have to be a team player, so I always try to keep a lid on any frustration and just go with the flow. I don't want to be a burden on the guys. Is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm answering that right, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Before age 12, did you have problems with attention, impulsivity, or being overly restless?

Um, yeah... I guess it's been going on for a while. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a troublemaker or anything, because I really wasn't trying to be a bad kid. But, well, my mom says I was pretty much exactly like this back in grade school, too. 

She said I was always out of my seat, or, you know, just blurting out answers in class before the teacher was done talking. And I was always losing my homework... she got a fair amount of notes sent home from my teachers, which I always felt really guilty about. They always made sure to tell her I was bright enough to do the work, though, so it wasn't that I couldn't learn it. I just... had a hard time keeping it all together, I guess. 

Am I giving you the right kind of background? I just want to make sure this is helpful for you.
Have you been using any stimulants, such as cocaine, methamphetamine, or non-prescribed ADHD medication, lately?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I mean, with my job, we get drug tested pretty regularly anyway, but even if we didn't, I just... I wouldn't do that. I know some people might think that firefighters have this crazy, wild culture, but I really try to keep my nose clean and just focus on doing a good job. I don't even take anything that's not prescribed to me, honestly. I hope that's the right answer... I mean, it's the truth, I just want you to know I take my health and my job really seriously. Is that okay?
Have you had any period of at least several days where you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Oh, no, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I mean, obviously, with the shifts at the firehouse, sometimes my sleep schedule gets a little... unpredictable? Like, we might be up half the night on a call. But when that happens, I'm definitely exhausted the next day. I never have those times where I just don't need sleep and still feel totally energized. 

I really try to prioritize getting enough rest when I'm off duty so I can be at my best for the crew. I'd hate to be dragging on the job and let anyone down, you know? So, yeah, if I don't sleep, I definitely feel it like anyone else would. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right for you.
Have these symptoms been causing problems in more than one area of your life, like at work and at home?

Um... yeah. I guess it has. I mean, at home, things get a little disorganized, which I always feel terrible about. But... work is the part that really, really bothers me. 

I hate even admitting this to you, because I really pride myself on being a good firefighter and a good team player, but... well, it’s started costing me some trust at the firehouse. I actually got pulled into a performance and safety meeting recently. I mean, they were really nice about it, they weren't yelling or anything, but... they basically said the crew can't always count on me to track the details consistently. 

And that just kills me, you know? I've been working so hard, and now my shot at moving into leadership feels like it’s slipping away because of all this. I just really want to fix it so I don't let my team down. Am I making sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for, I just want to be totally honest with you.
Did these attention and restlessness problems continue into adulthood without a long symptom-free period?

Um, well, it hasn't always been this bad. I mean, I've always been a little energetic, maybe a bit scattered sometimes, but I usually managed it okay. I always wanted to be the guy who was ready for anything, you know? But... it’s really become a, well, a real problem for about a year and five months now. 

That’s when they changed our schedule to these longer rotating shifts, and they added a bunch of extra documentation and, um, drone duties for me to handle. I was really honored they trusted me with the drone stuff, I really was, but... ever since then, I just can't seem to keep all the plates spinning. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm making excuses or blaming the job, because I'm not. I know I should be able to handle it. Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
When these problems got worse about a year and five months ago, were you going through a major stressor or life change?

Um... no, not really. I mean, besides the schedule change and the new duties at the firehouse that I mentioned, there wasn't really anything else going on. My personal life has been pretty steady, thankfully. My wife is super supportive, and things at home are... well, they're good. 

I really don't want it to seem like I'm just stressed out and can't handle my life, you know? I mean, everyone deals with changes at work, and I should be able to adapt like the rest of the crew. I just... I don't know why I'm struggling so much with this specifically. I hope that's okay, that I don't have some big traumatic event to point to? I'm just trying to give you the most accurate picture I can.
Did your concentration and restlessness problems start only after the schedule and duty changes at work?

Um... well, actually, no. I mean, it definitely got a lot harder to manage recently, but... I guess I've always been a little bit like this? I hate to admit it, but my mom was just telling me the other day that I was exactly like this back in grade school. 

She said I was always bouncing out of my seat, or, um, blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking the question. And I guess I lost my homework a lot, too. She said she was always getting notes sent home about it, which I feel awful about, putting her through that. She always said I was bright enough to do the work, I just... couldn't seem to stay on track. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker. I always tried to be good, I promise. I just had a lot of energy. Is that... is that the kind of history you need to know? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right pieces.
Did these attention and restlessness problems cause clear difficulty in your functioning before the recent work schedule change, or only after it?

Um, well... I guess I'd say it really only started causing major problems *after* the schedule change. Like I said, I always managed okay before. But lately... it's gotten pretty bad. 

I really hate to even say this, because I love my crew and I don't want you to think I'm a bad firefighter, but... I was actually pulled into a performance and safety meeting recently. It was awful. I felt like I let everyone down. It's just that I've been missing details, and... well, it's starting to cost me their trust. I've been working so hard to move into a leadership role, and now it feels like that's just slipping away because they can't count on me to stay on top of things. 

I'm really trying my best to fix it, I promise. I don't want to be the weak link. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not oversharing or making it sound worse than it is... I just want you to understand where I'm at right now.
Do you notice these attention and restlessness problems mainly when you're dealing with changes or pressure at work, or do they happen even when things are calm?

Um... well, it's not just at work, honestly. I wish it was, because then I could just leave it at the station, you know? But... it happens even when things are completely calm. 

Like, even on my days off, when I'm just supposed to be relaxing with my wife and kids. I really try to just sit down and do quiet stuff with them, like watch a movie or play a board game, because I know they like that. But... I don't know, I just have such a hard time staying put. I'll start talking too much, or I'll get up before we've even been sitting that long. I always end up wandering out to the garage to check on my tools, or just moving around the house doing... whatever. 

I feel terrible about it, because I don't want my family to think I don't want to spend time with them. I love them so much, and I really want to be a good husband and dad. I just... I get so antsy when things are too quiet. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad family man. I'm really trying to be better about it. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
